title.rendered: Sinopia Biosciences Receives $2.5M NIH Grant

content.rendered:
Sinopia Biosciences, Inc., a San Diego, CA-based biotechnology company, has been awarded a $2.5m Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Phase II grant from the National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS), part of the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

The award will support the development and validation of an AI-powered metabolomics foundation model designed to integrate data generated across different experimental platforms and analytical methods, enabling Sinopia to leverage diverse datasets for drug discovery through its proprietary LEADS® (LEarn And DiScover) platform.

Led by Aarash Bordbar, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer and co-founder, Sinopia is a biotechnology company leveraging multi-omics data, high-throughput screening, and artificial intelligence to identify and develop first-in-class therapies for diseases with significant unmet need.

The Phase II award builds on the company’s prior work developing a metabolomics foundation model, as well as large scale metabolomics profiling efforts spanning small molecules targeting more than 1,000 proteins across multiple cellular contexts. Under the new award, Sinopia will expand the foundation model using diverse proprietary and public datasets, expand drug perturbation profiling, and evaluate its ability to identify novel therapeutic targets and compounds in preclinical disease models.

Sinopia Biosciences is a biotechnology company leveraging multi-omics data, high-throughput screening, and artificial intelligence to discover and develop first-in-class therapies for diseases with significant unmet need. The company’s proprietary LEADS® (LEarn And DiScover) platform uncovers novel disease biology and targets to identify differentiated therapeutic opportunities. Sinopia’s pipeline is led by SB-0110, a novel PKA-II modulator in preclinical development for Parkinson’s disease, with additional discovery programs spanning multiple disease areas.

Sinopia is headquartered at JLABS San Diego.

title.rendered: Got a Raise, Bonus, or Windfall? The Money Mistakes Most People Make

content.rendered:
A big financial moment can feel like the end of a long climb, but in many ways it’s just the beginning.

Maybe you’ve landed a job with a much higher salary, received a generous year-end bonus, inherited money, or sold a home. Whatever the source, you now have more money to manage than ever before, and the decisions you make in the weeks that follow can shape your finances for years.

Most people put a great deal of thought into earning money and surprisingly little into managing it once it arrives. Work gets deadlines, plans, and regular check-ins, while personal finances get whatever attention is left at the end of the day. That imbalance leads to small, avoidable mistakes that often stay hidden until tax season, a job loss, or a major life change, when they become much harder and more expensive to fix.

Fortunately, these mistakes tend to follow a familiar pattern, and once you know what to look for, they’re easy to avoid.

Mistake One: Keeping All Your Money in One Place

Before you focus on growing your wealth, make sure the money you already have is protected and organized.

Relying on a Single Bank

After a large deposit, it’s common to leave everything in one checking account. That’s convenient, but it can expose you to unnecessary risk. The FDIC insures deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, for each account ownership category. If your balance goes beyond that limit, spreading your money across more than one bank or using different ownership categories keeps all of it protected.

Leaving Cash Idle

Money you won’t need for the next few months can earn a return without much risk. High-yield savings accounts, Treasury bills, and money market funds are all popular options. The point isn’t to chase big gains. It’s simply to keep your savings from losing value to inflation while it waits to be used.

Blending Every Goal Together

When your rent, vacation fund, and long-term savings all sit in the same account, it’s hard to know how much you can actually spend. Giving each goal its own account makes your money easier to track and much harder to spend by accident.

Mistake Two: Spending Too Quickly and Saving Too Little

Once your money is organized, the next step is deciding how to use it, and this is where good intentions often go off track.

Letting Lifestyle Creep Take Over

A bigger paycheck makes it tempting to upgrade everything at once, from your car and apartment to how often you eat out. Each change may seem minor on its own, but together they can quietly use up your entire raise. A simple habit can help: before you increase your spending, decide how much of the extra money will go toward savings, and set up automatic transfers so it happens without effort.

Skipping the Emergency Fund

Circumstances can change quickly. A layoff, an unexpected medical bill, or an urgent home repair can turn a comfortable month into a stressful one. Without an emergency fund, people are often pushed into hasty decisions, such as relying on credit cards or withdrawing from retirement accounts. Keeping several months of living expenses set aside gives you the breathing room to make thoughtful choices when you need them most.

Mistake Three: Overlooking Taxes

Spending and saving shape your finances today, but taxes are where small oversights can become costly, and many tax rules come with deadlines that offer no second chances.

Underestimating Your Tax Bill

Bonuses, freelance income, and investment gains don’t always have enough tax withheld. Many people only discover this when they file their return and find they owe more than expected, sometimes with penalties added. If your income has changed, review your withholding or set money aside for estimated tax payments so you aren’t caught off guard.

Missing Out on Tax-Advantaged Accounts

Retirement accounts such as a 401(k) or IRA, along with a health savings account if you’re eligible, can lower your taxes while helping you build long-term wealth. Each of these accounts has annual contribution limits and deadlines, and once a year’s window closes, that opportunity is usually gone for good. Even modest contributions, made consistently, can grow into far more than most people expect.

Selling Investments Without a Plan

How long you own an investment affects how it’s taxed. In the U.S., assets held for more than a year generally qualify for lower long-term capital gains rates, so selling just a few weeks too soon can noticeably increase your tax bill. Checking your purchase dates before you sell is a small step that can save you real money.

Forgetting About State Taxes

Where you live affects how much of your income and investment gains you get to keep, and moving to a different state can change your tax bill significantly. It’s worth understanding the basics before you make major decisions about where to live.

Mistake Four: Planning Only for the Best-Case Scenario

It’s natural to assume things will keep going well, but sound planning also prepares you for the times when they don’t.

Co-Signing Without Understanding the Risk

Co-signing a loan or lease for a friend or relative can feel like a generous gesture. However, if they can’t keep up with the payments, the debt becomes your responsibility and can damage your credit. Read every agreement carefully, make sure you understand exactly what you’re committing to, and only co-sign for an amount you could comfortably cover yourself.

Putting Off Estate Planning

Estate planning may seem unnecessary if you’re in your thirties, but it matters more than you might think. A basic will, up-to-date beneficiaries on your accounts, and adequate insurance coverage all help protect the people who depend on you. These steps are simple and affordable to take care of now, and much harder to arrange in the middle of a crisis.

Depending Too Heavily on One Source

If your paycheck, savings, and investments are all tied to the same employer or the same type of asset, a single setback can affect every part of your finances at once. Diversifying your investments gives you a foundation that doesn’t depend on any one outcome.

Why Good Financial Advice Pays for Itself

All of these mistakes have something in common: people are making important financial decisions without anyone reviewing them. That’s why getting sound advice early can make such a meaningful difference.

An experienced financial advisor can point out missed savings opportunities, warn you about risky commitments, and help you build a plan before small issues turn into larger ones. Still, many people feel too busy, too early in their careers, or too short on money to hire one. Fortunately, that gap is narrowing. Tools like an AI financial planner can help you work through budgets, savings goals, and everyday money questions at any time of day, so you arrive at a meeting with a professional already well prepared. For many people, the best approach combines both: convenient, on-demand guidance for routine questions and an expert for the complex, high-stakes decisions.

What matters most is having someone in your corner. You’d hire an inspector before buying a home or ask a lawyer to review an important contract, and your personal finances deserve the same level of care.

What to Look for in an Advisor

Look for someone with experience helping people in situations similar to yours, whether you’re managing a rising income, a sudden windfall, or planning for a growing family. Ask how they’re compensated. Fee-only advisors don’t earn commissions on the products they recommend, which removes a common source of bias. Finally, choose someone who explains things clearly. If you leave a meeting more confused than when you arrived, keep looking.

Conclusion

A raise, bonus, or windfall is an exciting milestone, but it also marks a period when even small financial choices can have lasting effects. The mistakes that hold people back are rarely dramatic. More often, they come from simple neglect, from being so focused on work and everyday life that personal finances slip through the cracks.

Organizing your money, keeping your spending in check, staying on top of tax deadlines, and preparing for more than one outcome all work together to strengthen your financial future. With good advice tying those pieces into a clear plan, you’ll be in a far better position, wherever life takes you next.

Hive serves over 1,600 clients including some of the world’s largest venues, promoters, festivals & artists.

title.rendered: Hola Prime Simplifies Prop Trading Rules With Launch Of It’s Rulebook

content.rendered:
New York, USA, October 21st, 2026, FinanceWire

The rulebook consolidates account requirements, removes three funded account restrictions and maintains transparent change logs so traders can track rule updates.

Hola Prime, a global proprietary trading firm, today announced the launch of The Rulebook, a consolidated rulebook designed to make trading rules and account conditions easier to access, understand and track.

The updated rulebook brings key information covering challenge passing criteria, conditions, trading rules, breach conditions and account requirements into one place. It also maintains transparent change logs, allowing traders to follow updates to the rules and understand how the firm’s requirements evolve over time.

By centralising this information, Hola Prime aims to give traders a clearer reference point throughout their trading journey, from understanding account conditions before trading to reviewing the rules that apply to their accounts.

All Rules in One Place, With Transparent Change Logs

Prop trading rules and account conditions play an important role in how traders manage their accounts. Having access to the applicable requirements in one place helps traders understand their obligations without having to navigate multiple resources.

The Rulebook brings these requirements together in a single document, giving traders one central reference for the rules governing their accounts. The rulebook is designed to make access to information more straightforward and give traders greater clarity on the requirements they are expected to follow.

Three Restrictions Removed

As part of the update, Hola Prime has removed three restrictions that previously applied to funded accounts:

  • The 60% maximum concentration per trade
  • The 70% maximum margin rule
  • The three-minute Stop Loss deadline

These changes form part of Hola Prime’s broader effort to simplify its trading conditions while making the applicable rules easier for traders to review.

A Clearer Process for Breach Appeals

While The Rulebook provides a central reference for trading rules and account conditions, Hola Prime also offers traders a way to challenge a breach they believe has been applied incorrectly.

Traders who have grounds to dispute a breach can submit an appeal through the available appeal process. Hola Prime’s Risk Team reviews the circumstances and provides a written explanation of the outcome, whether the original breach is upheld or reversed.

This process gives traders a formal channel to raise concerns and seek clarification when they believe an account decision does not align with the applicable rules.

Making Rule Transparency Part of the Trader Experience

Somesh Kapuria, CEO of Hola Prime, said: “Clear rules are an important part of a fair trading environment. Traders should be able to find the conditions that apply to their accounts without having to search across multiple resources. With The Rulebook, we are bringing those requirements together and maintaining transparent change logs so traders can keep track of updates. We have also removed three restrictions from Sim. funded accounts as part of our ongoing effort to make our trading conditions clearer and more straightforward.”

The Rulebook is available to Hola Prime traders on the official Hola Prime website.

About Hola Prime

Hola Prime is a global proprietary trading firm offering funded trading accounts to traders worldwide. The firm provides access to trading opportunities across major financial instruments, including forex, commodities and indices, with programs designed for different trading approaches.

Known for its 1-Hour Payout model, Hola Prime has received industry recognition, including the Global Most Transparent Prop Firm 2025 award by Finance Magnates and the Fastest Payout Prop Firm MEA 2026 award by UF Awards.

For more information, users can visit www.holaprime.com.

title.rendered: BillGo Is In Your Payment Network. Here’s What That Actually Means

content.rendered:
When a small business receives an unexpected call from a company called BillGO, the instinct is often suspicion. 

The name is unfamiliar. The caller says a payment is waiting. They cannot name the customer who sent it. For a business owner who has never heard of BillGO, none of that adds up.

The context is this: BillGO is not calling from outside the payment system your customers use. It is calling from inside it.

Understanding what that means, and why it matters, starts with understanding how bank payment networks actually work, and where companies like BillGO fit within them.

How Banks Deliver Bill Payments — and Where BillGO Fits In

When a customer logs into their bank’s website or mobile app to pay a bill, they are using a system their bank built and maintains. 

What most payers do not know is that behind that system sits a network of technology partners that help the bank route, deliver and confirm those payments.

Banks do not build every piece of that infrastructure themselves. BillGo partners with financial technology companies that specialize in specific parts of the payment delivery process. 

Those partnerships are formal, governed by contracts and subject to the compliance and security standards the bank requires of every vendor it works with.

BillGO is one of those partners. 

It operates one of the largest and open small business payments networks in the United States. BillGO works with financial institutions to ensure payments initiated through their bill pay systems can be delivered to small businesses digitally.

When BillGO contacts a small business, it is doing so because a payment initiated through one of those financial institution partnerships is ready to be delivered, and the business has not yet enrolled in the network that would deliver it. 

The call is not a cold outreach from an unknown company. It is a notification originating from inside a payment system the business’s own customers are already using.

Why BillGO Cannot Always Name the Bank or the Customer

This is the part of the BillGO outreach that most often generates confusion, and sometimes suspicion. A caller who says a payment is waiting but cannot name the sender sounds, understandably, like a red flag.

The reason BillGO cannot always disclose the name of the specific financial institution or the customer behind a payment is a standard confidentiality practice that governs how financial services partnerships operate.

When a bank partners with a technology company to help deliver payments, the terms of that partnership typically include restrictions on how the technology partner communicates with end users on the bank’s behalf. 

Disclosing specific customer or institution names without authorization from the bank would violate those terms. 

BillGO operates within those constraints because it is required to, not because it has anything to hide.

A company operating fraudulently does not have partnership agreements with financial institutions that include confidentiality provisions. It does not have compliance obligations to meet or contractual terms to honor. 

The very constraint that makes BillGO’s outreach feel opaque is evidence of a legitimate institutional relationship, not the absence of one.

Small business owners who have encountered this constraint and interpreted it as suspicious are not wrong to be cautious. But the explanation for it is institutional, not evasive, and it applies precisely because BillGO operates within the regulated infrastructure of the US payment system.

What Being Part of a Payment Network Means for Small Businesses

For a small business that has never thought about payment networks, the concept can feel abstract. Here is what it means in practical terms.

Every time one of your customers pays a bill through their bank or accounts payable platform, that payment enters a routing system. 

The system determines how the payment will be delivered to you. If your business is enrolled in a digital payment network like BillGO Exchange, BillGO’s biller network, the payment is delivered digitally on the same day. 

If your business is not enrolled, the payment is typically converted to a paper check and sent by mail, which can take seven to ten days to arrive.

The customer has already paid either way. The difference is entirely in how long it takes the money to reach you.

Enrolling in BillGO Exchange does not require your customers to change anything about how they pay. They continue using the same bank portal they always have. 

The change happens on the delivery side, and the result is that payments that previously arrived by mail begin arriving digitally, on the day they are sent.

How to Confirm BillGO Is Legitimate

If BillGO has contacted your business and you want to verify the company independently before enrolling, that is exactly the right approach. 

BillGO’s company information, network details and contact information are available at billgo.com. You can look the company up, call back on a number you find yourself and ask any questions you have before moving forward.

What you will find is a company with deep roots in the US financial services ecosystem, formal relationships with financial institutions and payment providers across the country, and more than 100 thousand small business customers who receive payments through its network every day.

Legitimate payment companies do not ask you to send money, share your online banking login or password, or pay a fee to receive funds that are already owed to you. BillGO does none of those things. 

Enrollment in BillGO Exchange is at no additional cost to the business. BillGO partners with financial institutions and payment providers to offer this service.

The verification process is simple and the information is publicly available. A company that has nothing to hide does not discourage scrutiny. BillGO welcomes it.

The Outreach Is the First Step, Not the Last

For many small businesses, the BillGO call is the beginning of a short conversation that ends with faster payments and less time spent waiting on the mail. 

For others, the unfamiliarity of the outreach leads them to decline before they understand what is being offered.

The goal of this piece is to make sure that decision, whichever way it goes, is made with accurate information. 

BillGO is calling from inside your payment ecosystem, on behalf of a customer who has already sent you money, through a bank that has already processed the transaction, through a network that is ready to deliver it the moment you enroll.

The payment system your customers use every day already includes BillGO. Enrollment is simply the step that connects your business to the part of that system designed to pay you faster.

title.rendered: Why Bingo Is the Overlooked Vertical in UK iGaming Investment Analysis

content.rendered:
UK iGaming investor attention concentrates on two verticals. Sports betting dominates coverage, with casino sitting a close second. Bingo rarely makes the deck.

That reporting pattern misses a stable, cash-generative segment of the UK regulated market. UK bingo operators run established business models with mature player bases, predictable retention curves, and clear platform economics. The vertical deserves more analytical attention than it currently receives.

What the Market Data Actually Shows

UK bingo accounts for roughly 5 to 7 percent of UK online gambling gross gaming revenue in a mature year. The segment is smaller than sports betting or online casino, which is partly why it attracts less investor attention. But the growth trajectory and margin profile tell a different story from what the headline revenue figures suggest.

Bingo operators run high customer lifetime values compared with sports betting and casino verticals. Player retention curves are longer. Customer acquisition costs are lower because the vertical attracts a defined demographic through word-of-mouth and community features rather than paid search competition against the volume keywords that drive casino and sports betting CAC up.

Industry data from H2 Gambling Capital’s UK market research shows bingo revenue holding steady year over year, with online growth offsetting modest declines in the land-based hall segment. The combined trajectory keeps the vertical in positive territory even as the market reconfigures around digital delivery.

Operator Landscape and Platform Economics

The UK online bingo operator landscape splits into three structural categories. Vertically integrated bingo-first operators run their own platforms and brands, while white-label platforms deliver bingo infrastructure that multi-vertical operators layer their own branding onto. Multi-vertical operators carry bingo as one of several products alongside casino and sports betting.

The Rank Group, Buzz Bingo, Jackpotjoy, and tombola occupy the bingo-first category. Each runs significant hall estates alongside online operations. ProgressPlay and Jumpman Gaming operate white-label platforms that power dozens of mid-tier operator brands in the UK regulated market.

The multi-vertical operator category covers brands that carry bingo alongside casino and sports betting products. The growth of multi-vertical platforms across European regulated markets is documented in earlier coverage of the expanding European iGaming market, with bingo often appearing as a cross-sell segment that extends the operator’s demographic reach.

The Multi-Vertical Operator Pattern in Practice

The multi-vertical operator pattern runs through platforms such as Fruity King Bingo, a UK operator carrying the vertical alongside its casino and sports betting products. The platform runs on the ProgressPlay infrastructure, with bingo appearing as one segment of the broader catalog rather than the primary product.

The economics of this configuration are different from a bingo-first operator. Customer acquisition costs are shared across verticals, and bingo often serves as a lower-intensity entry product that cross-sells into higher-margin casino games later in the player lifecycle. For investors modeling multi-vertical operator economics, the bingo contribution is often undermodeled relative to its actual retention and cross-sell value.

UK Bingo Vertical: Investor Reference Points

5-7%   share of UK online gambling GGY attributable to bingo in a mature year

3   structural operator categories (bingo-first, white-label, multi-vertical)

40%+   typical player retention rate advantage for bingo versus casino verticals

Low   paid-search CAC relative to sports betting and casino segments

Why the Vertical Keeps Getting Overlooked

Bingo’s low profile in investor analysis has several causes. The vertical is dominated by a handful of established UK operators with limited public-market activity compared with the sports betting and casino segments, which produces thin deal flow and less analyst coverage. The player demographic skews older and less tech-forward, which does not fit the growth narratives that attract venture capital attention.

The vertical also lacks the regulatory controversy that drives attention to sports betting and casino. Bingo has not been the focus of the same intensity of advertising restrictions, affordability checks debate, or problem gambling framing that have reshaped the other UK verticals. Less controversy produces less news coverage.

None of this changes the underlying economics. Bingo remains a cash-generative vertical with mature customer economics and defensible operator positions. The analytical gap between coverage volume and actual segment value is where overlooked investment opportunities tend to form, and the UK bingo vertical fits that profile cleanly.

title.rendered: What Should You Consider Before Selling a High-Performing Investment?

content.rendered:
A big gain on an investment feels great, and selling it can feel tempting. Before you click the sell button, a few questions deserve a clear answer. After an investment that has gained a lot is sold, taxes often take more of the profit than expected.

At EP Wealth Advisors, the review goes past performance numbers to what a sale costs in taxes. That closer look matters because a sale cannot be undone once it settles. When an investor weighs the tax cost before the trade goes through, more of the profit stays put.

Why Gains Create a Tax Bill

You owe tax on the profit, meaning the sale price minus your original cost. A stock bought at $20 and sold at $50 leaves a $30 gain. By choosing when to sell, an investor often keeps more of that profit away from the tax bill. Federal tax is only one layer, since many states also tax investment gains. Higher earners may also owe an extra surtax called the net investment income tax. A large sale can push your income into a higher bracket for that year.

How Holding Time Changes the Rate

How long you owned the investment can change your tax rate by a lot. Gains on assets held one year or less are taxed as ordinary income. An investment held longer than a year usually qualifies for lower long-term capital gains rates. Those long-term rates are 0, 15, or 20 percent, depending on your income. Waiting a few extra weeks to pass the one year mark can save thousands. Always confirm your exact purchase date before you decide when to sell it.

Offsetting Gains With Losses

Losing investments can quietly work in your favor when you sell a winner. Capital losses are applied against capital gains first, and matching gains are offset before any others. Any losses left over after that reduce a taxpayer’s ordinary income by up to $3,000 each year. Whatever exceeds that limit rolls over into later tax years, and the carryover never expires. Intentionally selling losing positions to offset your gains is known as tax loss harvesting. Repurchasing that investment within 30 days before or after triggers the wash sale rule.

Weighing Risk and Concentration

Taxes are only half the story, because overloading on one asset adds risk. A winner that grows quickly can become a large share of your portfolio. If that one holding drops sharply, your whole financial plan can feel the hit. Some investors sell in stages over several years to spread out the tax impact. Others keep the position but direct new savings elsewhere to rebalance the portfolio gradually. When the money is needed in a few years, the investor plans around that timeline, regardless of recent returns.

Other Ways to Lower the Bill

Donating appreciated shares directly to a charity can avoid the capital gains tax entirely. Donor advised funds make this easier by letting you give over several years. Heirs who inherit investments usually get a stepped up basis that erases past gains. Selling in a lower income year can also mean a lower tax rate. Early retirement years, before other income begins, are sometimes ideal for selling big winners. A tax professional can model each option before you commit to a trade.

Before You Hit Sell

Selling a winner doesn’t have to feel like a gamble with your tax bill. Before selling, an investor spends a day matching the purchase date and original cost against this year’s income. Those three numbers usually tell you more than any market headline ever will. Once the purchase date and cost are confirmed, the investor sees the likely tax bill before placing the order. A steep bill sometimes sends the sale into a later year when income runs lower. The account owner makes the final decision, and the tax numbers are already on the table by then.

title.rendered: 4 VC Firms for B2B Tech Startups in 2027: Product Signals or ARR?

content.rendered:
B2B tech startups receive funding from venture capital firms that evaluate early evidence through different diligence lenses.

Some firms use product signals to understand adoption, engagement, and product-led demand before financial metrics fully mature, while others place more emphasis on ARR, go-to-market progress, team quality, market opportunity, or enterprise execution.

That distinction matters at pre-seed and seed, when annual recurring revenue (ARR) may be limited or absent. Choosing an investor starts with understanding what the business can demonstrate today.

How Do Investors Evaluate B2B Tech Startups?

Investors evaluate B2B tech startups by matching the company’s current evidence to the stage of the round. At pre-seed and seed, that evidence may include product adoption, customer feedback, usage depth, GTM progress, team quality, market timing, and early revenue where available.

Product Signals vs. Financial Metrics

Product signals show how customers respond to a tool: how quickly adoption spreads, how deeply users engage, whether they recommend it and how usage translates into interest in paying.

Financial indicators show the commercial results of that behavior. ARR measures recurring revenue on an annualized basis. Revenue growth, customer retention and sales efficiency help investors assess whether demand supports a sustainable business. GTM progress shows how a company reaches and converts customers.

Product behavior can reveal momentum before financial patterns mature. Adoption velocity, engagement depth, user advocacy and conversion behavior can all provide useful evidence at this stage. Repeated use can provide stronger evidence than registrations followed by inactivity. ARR remains important as the business develops.

What Changes at Pre-Seed and Seed Stage

At pre-seed, founder insight, market timing, customer feedback and early product behavior may carry considerable weight because little revenue history exists.

At seed, investors may have more adoption, retention and commercial data to examine. Expectations still depend on the business model and product maturity. An enterprise tool with long purchasing cycles will produce evidence differently from self-service software.

Founders should ask which proof points matter to the specific partner evaluating their company. The same startup can present differently through a product-usage, SaaS-metric or GTM lens.

4 VC Firms for B2B Tech Startups

Mighty Capital, a16z, Bessemer, and Accel each show a different way investors assess early B2B tech momentum, from product signals to ARR, GTM progress, and enterprise execution.

Mighty Capital

Mighty Capital is an early-stage, B2B-specialist venture capital firm built for B2B tech founders raising from pre-seed through Series A. That focus matters because pre-seed and seed founders need investors whose check size, lead role, and support model match the stage where product evidence often develops before ARR fully matures.

Mighty Capital invests at pre-seed through Series A in B2B technology companies with enterprise ambitions, writing checks from $200K to $5M+ and leading most rounds, providing founder-friendly terms and direct operational support from the product leadership network, a specialist alternative to generalist multi-stage funds.

Its evaluation model supports that early-stage focus. Mighty Capital is a venture capital firm that invests in B2B technology companies using the Product Alpha Effect™, a proprietary methodology that reads product signals from 600,000+ product leaders to identify outlier companies before traditional investors do. Its Product Signal Stack examines adoption velocity, engagement depth, community advocacy and product-qualified lead (PQL) conversion patterns.

Through its exclusive Products That Count partnership, Mighty Capital reads early product signals from 600,000+ CPOs and product managers. The community also provides structured buyer distribution for portfolio companies, helping founders sell more and faster.

Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)

Andreessen Horowitz is a broad, multi-stage technology investment platform operating from seed through growth across areas including enterprise software, AI, infrastructure and fintech. Its scale brings operating resources spanning talent, marketing, legal and policy support.

For B2B founders, that breadth can be useful when the pitch depends on a large market, a strong founding team, technical differentiation and the potential to scale across a major technology category. Available traction helps explain the opportunity, but early-stage investing does not require waiting for mature ARR.

a16z is generalist and platform-driven rather than built around a proprietary product-signal methodology. Founders should establish which team fits their business and what evidence that team expects at the current stage.

The practical attraction is brand recognition, portfolio breadth and access to a wide operating network. Its fit is strongest for founders who want multi-stage platform support rather than a specialist pre-seed-through-Series-A B2B investor.

Bessemer Venture Partners

Bessemer Venture Partners brings established cloud, SaaS, and B2B software expertise to this comparison. Its strength is not a product-signal methodology, but a long-running software investment lens that helps founders frame commercial performance once customer and revenue data begin to matter.

For B2B software startups with emerging ARR, Bessemer’s SaaS and cloud guidance can make metrics more legible. Repeatable sales cycles, retention, acquisition efficiency, and net revenue retention help show whether demand is turning into a scalable business rather than remaining early interest.

That makes Bessemer especially relevant when a startup’s strongest evidence includes SaaS economics, cloud-market fit, and early commercial execution. It can suit founders ready to explain how customer demand is becoming measurable revenue, particularly as the company moves beyond initial product adoption into a more repeatable growth motion.

Accel

Accel brings B2B and enterprise investing experience to startups where go-to-market progress, customer targeting and early commercial execution are becoming central to the story. Its strength in this comparison is not product-signal diligence before metrics mature, but a broader enterprise lens for understanding how product demand turns into repeatable growth.

For B2B founders, that makes pilot outcomes, purchasing behavior, early revenue and sales motion useful evidence in the pitch. A company can show who uses the product, who pays for it, how customers are being reached and whether that route to market is becoming more consistent.

Accel’s early-stage activity also includes pre-product and pre-revenue companies through programs such as Atoms, so it is not limited to startups with mature ARR. Still, its positioning fits founders whose evidence is moving toward GTM traction, enterprise adoption and commercial development rather than primarily early product behavior.

How Should Founders Choose Between Product-Signal and ARR-Focused VCs?

The right fit depends on what the startup can already prove and which type of evidence an investor is best equipped to assess.

If a founder needs a specialist B2B tech investor for pre-seed through Series A, Mighty Capital writes $200K to $5M+ checks, leads most rounds and uses the Product Alpha Effect™ to evaluate early product evidence before ARR fully matures.

A founder looking for a broad multi-stage platform will find a16z suitable because of its scale, operating resources and coverage across multiple technology categories.

If a startup already has enough recurring-revenue and customer data for SaaS metrics to be meaningful, Bessemer’s cloud expertise helps frame retention, growth and commercial performance.

When GTM progress, pilot results or early revenue are the strongest proof points, Accel fits founders looking for enterprise and B2B experience tied to commercial execution.

Founders should start with their strongest evidence, then ask which investor is most likely to understand it.

Choosing the Right B2B Tech Investor

Before sending a pitch, founders can assemble usage data, customer feedback, GTM progress and available financial results into a clear account of what the company has proved.

Match that evidence to the investor’s questions, then establish what the partnership would contribute to the next stage of development. The strongest fundraising target is usually the investor whose diligence lens matches that evidence.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Product Signals Do VCs Look at Before Revenue?

Investors may examine adoption velocity, engagement depth, user advocacy, retention and conversion behavior. They also look at who uses the product and which problem it solves. Repeat usage and customer recommendations can reveal demand, but different investors weigh these signals differently.

Is ARR Necessary to Raise a Seed Round?

ARR is not universally required for seed funding. Expectations vary with the investor, business model, stage and product maturity. A company without recurring revenue may demonstrate its potential through customer validation, retention, technical progress or a credible market opportunity.

What Is the Difference Between Pre-Seed and Seed Funding for B2B Tech Startups?

Pre-seed often supports initial product development and validation, with evidence centered on the team, market and early customer response. Seed generally involves more proof of adoption, GTM development or commercial traction.

title.rendered: What Investors Should Know Before Investing in Canadian Physical Silver

content.rendered:
Silver doesn’t pay a dividend. You can’t buy anything in the grocery store with it, and if it is kept in the house it won’t grow. But people still buy it.

Why? Partly because it’s something they can have to themselves. But investing in real silver is a little more complicated than just picking out a coin and hoping its value rises.

What you see isn’t what you pay

Silver is a commodity you can invest in and is traded on the market in troy ounces. That will change through the trading day and it may not be the amount you really pay if you go out and acquire the metal.

If you want to buy silver in Canada you will find coins and bars of different sizes and even if they have the same silver content they will cost different amounts.

Premiums can blow the deal. Dealers also charge for manufacturing, handling and other commercial costs. Buyers love certain things more. And that’s what they charge you for extra. For example, a 1 ounce coin could cost more per ounce than a larger bar. But that doesn’t mean the bar is the better choice. Depends on what you want to do with the silver and what you are willing to spend.

Coins or bars? That’s what you do

If you walk into a bullion shop you will find silver in all shapes and all sizes. Coins are easy to identify, and there are only so many different ones. And what makes them hot. For example, the Royal Canadian Mint makes Canadian Maple Leaf silver coins. Another choice is bars, particularly for larger purchases. They can be cheaper per ounce but who knows? 

The Royal Canadian Mint has some advice for people who want to buy bullion, including shopping around among dealers and knowing the spot price. Just be careful of one thing, buy price and sale price are not the same. If you want to sell tomorrow, the dealer will give you a lot less. He can tell you a price now.

Where are you going to put it?

And some of us wait for our silver to do it. Save a few bucks. Easy. But a few huge bars is a different story. Silver is a pain to lug. You don’t want to be worried about theft and fire and if your insurance covers precious metals. A bank safe deposit box or professional storage facility can be an option, but these can add to the cost.

But that’s not the only real storage problem. If you are looking to sell you need to find a buyer that will give you a price you are comfortable selling your silver at. Depending on the buyer, this could be going to a dealer, arranging delivery or presenting paperwork.

Silver prices do not always rise

Silver is especially important for industry, above all in electronics and solar technology. So it has a different demand profile from gold. Prices are not being pushed up by industrial demand.

Silver is fluid. It is subject to economic conditions, on the opinion of investors and on changes in demand. In Canada silver is usually priced in U.S. dollars, so Canadian buyers must take into account exchange rates. Someone who buys now may see his investment fall in the next month. You can lose money on the dealer margin and selling charges even if the market price does not change.

But then Sell It, it’s easy to focus on the buy

Which coin is more beautiful? Is the premium worth it? Now? Or after? But the more interesting question is: what then happens? If you needed the cash could you sell it in 6 months and not lose a tonne? Now what are you gonna do? And will your cash get commingled with your savings and investments?

Adding real silver to a more diversified investment portfolio. Don’t expect it to save you money either. And you need to think a little bit about what you’re paying for and what you’re going to get back.

title.rendered: Origin Raises $20M in Funding

content.rendered:
Origin, a San Francisco, CA-based full-stack physical AI company building general-purpose robots for interior construction, emerged from stealth with $20m in total funding.

The round was co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures with participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures, Z21, ISAI and Imad Ventures, alongside angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla.

The company intends to use the funds to deploy OG-1, its flagship robot, and build out its fleet, support large-scale pilots with customers in the U.S. and Europe—including large drywall finishing contractors in the U.S., with additional pilots scheduled in Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia—and extend the platform to new interior trades.

Founded in early 2025 by Yogesh Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, Origin is building robots to help crews increase capacity, deliver consistently and turn that demand into revenue. OG-1, the company’s flagship robot, is designed to perform multiple interior construction trades on a single platform. Today, it autonomously completes wall-finishing workflows without human intervention. It applies compound, sands and primes walls to a professional finish. OG-1 can work long shifts and  handle complex tasks, from targeted spraying and finishing high walls to handling difficult areas like corners, pillars, soffits and edges, and it’s already delivering the quality expected of a skilled professional.

Built for rough, chaotic construction sites and uneven surfaces,  OG-1 moves on a three-wheeled platform and has a 360-degree view of its surroundings. It can work at heights of up to 14 feet and handle contact-rich tasks, such as sanding, using real-time force control to keep consistent pressure against the wall. OG-1 is designed to work safely alongside construction crews while other trades continue on sites, without requiring a separate cordoned-off work area.

OG-1 is powered by Origin’s Construction Action Model, a foundation model built specifically for construction. It brings together three core components:

  • A reasoning system that plans and orchestrates complex sub-tasks in the construction workflows
  • An action policy that enables OG-1 to navigate autonomously, identify exactly where to work, determine how to use each tool and assess the quality of its work
  • A controller that translates the policy’s actions through precise, feedback-driven control of the robot

Together, these components enable OG-1 to apply compound, sand, prime walls or do other construction tasks, adapting to changing site conditions. The model is trained using high-fidelity simulation and deployment data from live job sites. It enables OG-1 to generalize across different construction tasks and environments, transferring learned capabilities between workflows and adapting to variations in site conditions. Origin uses data from ongoing deployments to improve the model’s capabilities, performance and generalisation across tasks and environments over time.

Today, OG-1 is being deployed across commercial spaces, multi-family apartments, data centers, hotels and warehouses. Origin’s platform is ready for manufacturing at scale, and the company is targeting 150 robots deployed by the end of 2027. It plans to support additional interior trades like taping, drywall installation, drilling & conduit installation, using the same hardware platform and Construction Action Model.

Quick Summary: Core Market Structure Concepts

Market structure represents the organizational architecture and interactive mechanics governing how buyers and sellers transact within an economic or financial marketplace. It determines pricing power, liquidity distribution, regulatory oversight, and order execution speed. In contemporary financial markets, analyzing market structure allows institutional and retail traders to decode order book dynamics, locate resting limit orders, and observe algorithmic behavior. At Bookmap, we translate abstract market structure into an intuitive, high-definition visualization of liquidity and order flow, enabling traders to make informed, data-driven decisions.

Market Organization

Market organization defines the internal structural framework, exchange protocols, and settlement procedures that dictate how assets are exchanged. It outlines whether an asset class functions via a centralized clearing house—such as the London Stock Exchange (LSE) or Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME)—or within a decentralized, over-the-counter (OTC) bilateral network.

A transparent market organization minimizes systemic counterparty risk, ensures clear price discovery, and provides structured participant tiers ranging from retail brokerages to primary liquidity providers. Understanding this structural architecture is essential for assessing where volume gathers and where orders match. Bookmap maps the full depth of market organization visually, transforming raw data feeds from centralized exchanges into real-time visual heatmaps that pinpoint resting liquidity clusters.

Traders looking to navigate complex organizational layers can get started with dedicated tools configured for live exchange feeds.

Market Characteristics

Market characteristics encompass the operational traits that define price action and liquidity behavior across financial instruments. These characteristics include:

  • Tick size and lot granularity: The minimum price fluctuation and trade sizing permitted by an exchange.
  • Order book depth: The cumulative volume of bids and offers stacked across sequential price levels.
  • Latency and matching engine speeds: The millisecond and microsecond turnaround times of centralized matching algorithms.
  • Participation diversity: The balance between automated high-frequency trading (HFT) algorithms, institutional asset managers, market makers, and retail swing traders.

Monitoring these market characteristics provides critical context regarding asset volatility and the true cost of execution. When slippage increases during volatile sessions, assessing order book density reveals whether liquidity is genuinely available or merely fleeting.

Microeconomics Concepts

Market structure builds directly upon core microeconomics concepts that govern resource allocation, price formation, and participant incentives. Foundational principles include:

  1. Supply and Demand Elasticity: How sensitive buyer and seller participation remains when prices fluctuate.
  1. Marginal Cost vs. Marginal Revenue: The theoretical equilibrium points at which production or inventory holding ceases to yield additional profit.
  1. Information Asymmetry: Situations where institutional participants access deeper order flow data faster than everyday market participants.

In modern electronic trading, microeconomics concepts translate directly into order queue dynamics. For instance, when supply at a specific offer exhausts faster than incoming bids, upward price movement becomes mechanically inevitable. Visualizing this microeconomic balance in real time eliminates guesswork, bridging the gap between economic theory and live trade execution.

Economic Systems

Economic systems provide the macroeconomic, regulatory, and legal environments in which market structures function. Whether operating in a free-market economy, a mixed economy, or a strictly regulated state-directed model, the broader economic system determines capital flow, taxation, monetary policy, and competitive freedom.

  • Free-Market Systems: Encourage open access, decentralized capital allocation, and unregulated pricing driven strictly by competitive forces.
  • Mixed Economies: Predominant across modern Western nations, balancing private enterprise with regulatory protections like MiFID II in the UK and Europe or SEC regulations in the United States.
  • Regulated Financial Ecosystems: Impose capital requirements, short-selling restrictions, and reporting standards to prevent systemic liquidity crises.

Understanding how macro economic systems interact with exchange rules gives market participants a broader perspective on institutional risk management and macroeconomic capital cycles.

How Does Market Structure Affect Pricing?

Market structure dictates pricing power, execution efficiency, and spread stability across all trading venues. In highly fragmented environments—such as equities trading across multiple lit venues, multilateral trading facilities (MTFs), and dark pools—pricing can experience micro-discrepancies.

Key ways market structure influences real-time pricing include:

  • Bid-Ask Spread Compression: Competitive market structures with numerous liquidity providers naturally narrow the spread, lowering execution friction.
  • Liquidity Voids: In oligopolistic environments, sudden liquidity withdrawals by primary market makers cause rapid spread expansion and sharp price slippage.
  • Iceberg and Hidden Orders: Dominant institutions use structural order types to mask large purchases or disposals without prematurely alerting the broader market.

Using Bookmap, traders can see directly through these structural layers. By displaying real-time Limit Order Book (LOB) data as a continuous heatmap, Bookmap highlights resting iceberg orders, absorption patterns, and genuine market liquidity before price moves.

Perfect Competition Characteristics

Perfect competition serves as the theoretical gold standard of operational efficiency. Its primary characteristics include:

  • A large pool of small, independent buyers and sellers who cannot individually influence price.
  • Completely identical, homogeneous products or standardized contracts.
  • Zero barriers to market entry or exit.
  • Perfect, symmetrical information distributed instantaneously across all market actors.
  • Absence of transaction costs, brokerage fees, or regulatory friction.

While pure textbook perfect competition rarely exists, standardized financial futures markets—such as CME E-mini S&P 500 or Treasury bond contracts—closely reflect perfect competition characteristics. Here, standardized contracts, deep liquidity pools, and instant electronic dissemination foster aggressive price competition among millions of daily market orders.

Monopoly and Oligopoly Differences

Understanding monopoly and oligopoly differences is critical when analyzing pricing control and institutional consolidation within specific sectors.

A monopoly exists when an individual entity controls the entire market for a good or service, possessing unmatched pricing power and protected by insurmountable barriers to entry (such as legal patents, infrastructure ownership, or regulatory exclusivity). Monopolists can intentionally limit supply to keep consumer prices high.

An oligopoly, by contrast, features a small collective of powerful participants controlling the vast majority of market share. Rather than competing purely on price, these firms often exhibit strategic interdependence:

  • Price leadership, where one dominant firm sets the standard and others follow.
  • Heightened non-price competition through brand equity, exclusive distribution, and proprietary technology.
  • Susceptibility to tacit collusion, creating stable yet elevated pricing across an entire sector.

In financial trading, market-making consortiums in OTC foreign exchange often exhibit oligopolistic characteristics, concentrating order flow among a handful of tier-one investment banks.

Are You Looking for Market Structures in Economics or Finance?

When evaluating market structure, determining your domain context is vital:

  • In Economics: Market structure focuses on industry concentration, anti-trust regulation, societal deadweight loss, welfare distribution, and barriers to entry across consumer and industrial sectors.
  • In Finance and Trading: Market structure focuses on microstructure mechanics, including the Limit Order Book (LOB), algorithmic liquidity provision, clearing mechanisms, tick sizes, dark pools, and execution latency.

If you are a trader analyzing live charts, your priority is financial market microstructure: understanding where institutional orders sit, where stops are positioned, and how market makers balance inventory. Which Specific Industry Market Structure Are You Studying?

The operational dynamics of market structure vary dramatically depending on the specific sector or asset class under consideration:

  • Sovereign Debt and Commodities: Characterized by centralized institutional exchanges with heavy government participation and deep commercial hedging activities.
  • Equities and Derivatives: Heavily computerized, multi-exchange ecosystems driven by automated algorithms, smart order routers, and options-market gamma hedging.
  • Decentralized Finance (DeFi) & Digital Assets: Operated via automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pools and continuous peer-to-peer electronic order books, featuring unique slippage and gas-fee mechanics.
  • Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals: Highly monopolistic or oligopolistic environments protected by patent laws, clinical regulatory hurdles, and substantial capital expenditures.

Pinpointing your exact target market allows you to select the appropriate analytical framework, indicators, and data feeds.

5 Structural Indicators Every Trader Must Monitor

  1. Resting Liquidity Depth: The cumulative volume resting on the bid and ask sides across 20+ price levels.
  1. Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD): The net running total of market orders executed at the ask versus market orders executed at the bid, exposing aggressive absorption.
  1. Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP): The institutional benchmark reflecting the true average price paid per share or contract across the trading day.
  1. Order Book Imbalance (OBI): The real-time mathematical ratio comparing resting bids to resting offers, frequently preceding short-term directional breaks.
  1. Liquidity Sweeps and Absorption: Instances where large market orders consume all resting volume at a specific level without driving price further, signaling counterparty accumulation.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does market structure mean in simple terms?

In simple terms, market structure refers to the internal setup and rules of a marketplace, determining how many competitors operate, how easy it is to enter the space, and how prices are negotiated and settled.

How does Bookmap visualize market structure?

Bookmap visualizes market structure by translating the Limit Order Book into an intuitive, color-graded heatmap. Bright bands represent heavy resting limit orders (liquidity pools), while colored bubbles signify aggressive market orders executing in real time.

How do I know if an order book level is genuine or a spoof?

With Bookmap, you can monitor resting liquidity over time. If a large limit order disappears right before price reaches it, it was likely an algorithmic spoof intended to mislead participants. If price trades into the level and large volume bubbles confirm real execution, the liquidity was genuine.

Is Bookmap suitable for novice traders?

Yes. While institutional traders employ Bookmap for complex order flow strategies, beginners often find our visual heatmap substantially easier to interpret than traditional, fast-moving numerical DOM ladders or noisy candlestick patterns.

How does market structure impact day trading execution?

Market structure dictates whether you experience fast fills at expected prices or suffer severe slippage. By understanding where liquidity resides, day traders can place stop-losses behind genuine institutional size and enter positions where momentum is mechanically supported.

Can I practice with historical market data before trading live?

The company intends to use the funds to accelerate the development of its lead therapeutic candidate, DX5057, through Phase 1 and Phase 2 proof-of-concept clinical trials for patients with FSHD (facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy).

DX5057 is an orally administered small molecule inhibitor of DUX4 (double homeobox 4), a transcription factor whose aberrant expression in skeletal muscle drives FSHD. DX5057 is expected to distribute freely to all affected muscle and inhibit DUX4 deeply.

In connection with the financing, four new directors will join Altay’s board of directors: Ester Sklarsky, M.Sc., of Sound Bioventures; Carl Kilander, M.D., Ph.D., of HealthCap; Aidan King, MBA, of Fountain Healthcare Partners; and Chelsea Johnson, Ph.D., of Biogen New Ventures. title.rendered: INmune Bio Inc. and Quantum Computing Inc. Partner to Apply Quantum Optimization and AI to Advance Alzheimer’s Drug Research and Explore New Applications for XPro

content.rendered:
Boca Raton, Florida, October 14th, 2026, FinanceWire

  • Collaboration combines INmune Bio’s clinical research with QCi’s Dirac-3S quantum optimization machine to identify potential new treatment indications and biomarkers for XPro
  • Initial engagement marks QCi’s first commercial customer in pharmaceutical and biotechnology markets, expanding the application of quantum computing to drug development

INmune Bio Inc. (Nasdaq: INMB) and Quantum Computing Inc. (Nasdaq: QUBT) today announced a collaboration to apply quantum computing, artificial intelligence (AI) and data analytics to identify new potential applications for XPro (XPro1595), INmune Bio’s investigational treatment for Alzheimer’s disease and other disease conditions.

The collaboration brings together INmune Bio’s data from pre-clinical research through four clinical trials and understanding of disease biology with QCi’s Dirac-3S quantum optimization machine. Working with clinical and publicly available biomedical datasets, the companies intend to use quantum computing alongside AI and conventional data analytics to uncover relationships that could help find diseases driven by the same biology XPro targets, and to prioritize those with the greatest potential for success.

The Stage 1 engagement represents QCi’s first commercial customer in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology market. The agreement also provides options for additional work as INmune Bio advances its clinical development programs.

“We’ve built a large clinical dataset on Alzheimer’s and other diseases, backed by years of work with XPro,” said David Moss, Chief Executive Officer of INmune Bio. “This collaboration allows us to examine patient populations and biomarkers most likely to predict responses by analyzing large data sets. We’ll look for the diseases with the greatest potential for success, those whose human biology matches what we’ve already seen XPro do, starting with rare diseases where trials can be smaller, faster and more capital-efficient, and where qualifying pediatric approvals may earn a Priority Review Voucher.”

Together, the companies will build on INmune Bio’s research into XPro to explore where its approach to targeting inflammation may offer the greatest potential. XPro is designed to selectively inhibit soluble tumor necrosis factor (TNF), a protein involved in inflammation, while preserving other TNF functions important to the immune system. INmune Bio is investigating its potential in neurological and rare diseases where this targeted approach may offer a therapeutic benefit.

Using its Dirac-3S entropy quantum optimization machine alongside AI and conventional analytics, QCi will look for patterns and relationships across these datasets that could help researchers better understand treatment responses, identify promising patient populations and prioritize new indications for further study.

“This is a great example of what practical quantum computing can look like today,” said Yuping Huang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of QCi. “INmune Bio has a complex scientific problem and a substantial body of clinical and biological data. Our job is to bring new computing capabilities to that problem and see what we can learn. The potential to help researchers make better decisions about future treatments is exciting, and it opens an important new market for QCi.”

An important part of the program will be testing where quantum optimization adds value. The companies plan to compare results from QCi’s quantum optimization machine with appropriate conventional statistical and machine-learning methods, evaluating which approaches are best suited to different parts of the analysis.

The work is also intended to establish a repeatable discovery process through quantum computing that INmune Bio can use with additional datasets and potential disease indications.

For INmune Bio, the collaboration offers a new way to evaluate the broader potential of XPro and prioritize future development opportunities. For QCi, it represents an opportunity to showcase how its room-temperature, low-power quantum computing technology can be applied to complex, real-world problems in pharmaceutical research.

About INmune Bio Inc.

INmune Bio Inc. is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: INMB), late-stage biotechnology company focused on developing treatments that target the innate immune system to fight disease. The Company’s clinical-development strategy centers on advanced precision medicine, matching drug mechanisms directly to patient biology to optimize clinical outcomes.

INmune Bio is actively advancing two late-stage product platforms toward registrational milestones:

  • CORDStrom™: A proprietary, pooled, allogeneic, human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cell platform engineered to address the historical clinical challenges of donor variability and manufacturing inconsistency. Following successful clinical readouts in RDEB, the platform is transitioning to regulatory filing phases, with an MAA planned for the UK MHRA in 2026 and EU EMA in 2027, alongside a planned U.S. Biologics License Application (BLA) submission.
  • XPro1595™: A Dominant-Negative Tumor Necrosis Factor (DN-TNF) platform designed to selectively neutralize soluble TNF (sTNF) and reduce neuroinflammation without compromising protective immune function. Backed by recently granted FDA Fast Track designation and successful regulatory alignment from an End-of-Phase 2 meeting, XPro1595™ is positioned for an integrated Phase 2b/3 seamless adaptive registrational program in neuroinflammation-enriched early Alzheimer’s disease.

To learn more about INmune Bio’s pipeline and its approach to harnessing the innate immune system, please visit www.inmunebio.com.

About Quantum Computing Inc.

Quantum Computing Inc. (Nasdaq: QUBT) is an integrated quantum photonics company developing and manufacturing technologies that use light to compute complex information, capture hard-to-detect signals and communicate more securely. QCi brings together quantum optics, integrated photonics, semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging to create a more direct path from advanced science to practical products.

QCi’s portfolio includes quantum machines, photonic chips, components, modules and subsystems, as well as foundry and advanced manufacturing services. Its technologies are designed to operate at room temperature and low power, without the specialized cooling infrastructure required by many quantum approaches. These advantages enable deployment across computing and AI, secure communications, sensing and imaging, aerospace and defense, and other demanding applications.

Headquartered in Hoboken, New Jersey, QCi has operations across the United States. By combining advanced physics, device engineering and scalable manufacturing, QCi is working to make quantum and advanced photonic technologies more accessible and useful in the real world.

To learn more about QCi and its approach to harnessing light for practical quantum computing, please visit www.quantumcomputinginc.com.

title.rendered: Evolution Metals & Technologies Corp. Reaffirms $400 Million to $460 Million FY2027 Revenue Guidance, Unveils Eight Sintered Magnet Grades Covering an Estimated 75% of Global NdFeB Revenue, and Moves to Answer U.S. Army Call for Rare Earth Magnets

content.rendered:
Miami, Florida, October 14th, 2026, FinanceWire

Seven of eight grades customer-certified and first 13 of 57 containers of ULVAC equipment landed in Pohang on the path to more than 10,000 metric tons of annual capacity; SmCo production equipment targeted for mid-2027 as DFARS 252.225-7052 extends its mine-to-magnet restriction to SmCo magnets on January 1, 2027

Evolution Metals & Technologies Corp. (“EM&T” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: EMAT), a U.S.-based critical materials and advanced manufacturing company, today announced that its portfolio of eight sintered neodymium-iron-boron (“NdFeB”) rare earth magnet grades represents what the Company estimates to be approximately 75% of global sintered NdFeB magnet revenue and approximately 52% of global volume — placing EM&T squarely at the commercial center of the rare earth magnet market. The Company also reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $400 million to $460 million, announced that it expects to begin acquiring equipment to produce samarium cobalt (“SmCo”) magnets, the magnet class relied upon across U.S. military systems, by mid-2027, and confirmed it will respond to the U.S. Army’s sources sought notice for rare earth magnets.

The portfolio — N42SH, N48SH, N46SH, N35SH, N45H, N42H, N48M and N50M — spans the medium-, high- and super-high-temperature classes that drive the bulk of global magnet demand. Seven of the eight grades have already completed customer certification, led by N42SH, the single largest grade in the global market at an estimated 23% of sintered NdFeB revenue, now in commercial production at EM&T’s operations in Pohang, South Korea. The eighth grade, N48SH, is in the final stages of customer certification. Market share figures are Company estimates.

The portfolio’s revenue share exceeds its volume share by design: it is deliberately weighted toward the premium high-temperature grades that command the highest prices in the market. Its four super-high-temperature (“SH”) grades, rated to 150°C, incorporate heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium to hold their magnetic strength under extreme heat, and alone are estimated to represent approximately 49% of global sintered NdFeB revenue on just 30% of volume. These are the grades specified for EV traction motors, wind turbine generators, aerospace generators and defense actuators — the most demanding, highest-value applications in the industry.

With certification largely complete, EM&T’s priority for 2027 is scale. Thirteen additional ULVAC sintered magnet production machines are being delivered to Pohang, where the first 13 of 57 containers of ULVAC equipment have already arrived. The expansion is expected to lift annual capacity to more than 10,000 metric tons, including approximately 6,000 metric tons of high-performance sintered magnets, as the Company optimizes all eight grades for yield, consistency and throughput. On that foundation, EM&T reaffirms its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance of $10 million to $11 million and its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $400 million to $460 million.

The planned SmCo line extends EM&T into the magnet class at the heart of U.S. defense systems. SmCo magnets retain their performance at temperatures beyond the reach of NdFeB and deliver superior corrosion resistance and thermal stability, making them the standard choice for guidance and control systems, aerospace actuators, and radar and satellite systems. The timing is deliberate. Effective January 1, 2027, DFARS 252.225-7052 extends its restriction on SmCo magnets across the entire supply chain, from ore through finished magnet, for qualifying U.S. defense deliveries, while samarium itself has been subject to China’s rare earth export licensing controls since April 2025. Demand for compliant, non-China SmCo supply is building now. The line will draw on the expertise of Kenji Konishi, EM&T’s Head of Magnet Engineering Production and former Vice President and Chief Technology Officer of JL MAG Rare Earth, whose background spans sintered NdFeB and SmCo magnet systems from alloy design through mass production.

That demand is already surfacing at the federal level. On September 28, 2026, the U.S. Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Tobyhanna Division, issued a sources sought notice to identify potential vendors of rare earth magnets, with responses due October 28, 2026. EM&T will respond to the notice.

“EM&T will be answering the U.S. Army’s call for rare earth magnets,” said Andrew Knaggs, President of EM&T. “In a highly unusual move, the U.S. Army appears to intend to acquire magnets directly for its defense apparatus and contractors. With seven customer-certified grades in production in Pohang and a SmCo line on the way, we believe EM&T is exactly the kind of supplier that requirement is looking for.”

“Three quarters of the value in the global sintered magnet market sits in the eight grades EM&T produces, and our customers have already certified seven of them,” said David Wilcox, Executive Chairman of EM&T. “We did not build this portfolio around the edges of the market. We built it around the center, weighted toward the super-high-temperature grades that EV, wind, aerospace and defense customers specify and pay a premium for. 2027 is about execution: optimizing those eight grades as our new ULVAC capacity takes Pohang past 10,000 metric tons, and adding samarium cobalt, the magnet the U.S. defense industrial base depends on where heat and stability matter most. With DFARS reaching SmCo magnets on January 1, 2027 and samarium already under Chinese export licensing, demand for compliant supply is building now, and EM&T intends to meet it at commercial scale.”

“We are growing, and the proof is on the ground in Pohang,” said Frank Moon, Chief Executive Officer of EM&T. “The first 13 of 57 containers of ULVAC equipment have arrived, seven of our eight grades carry customer certification, and our fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $400 million to $460 million stands. These are not projections — they are milestones, and each one reflects production that is already scaling.”

“The grades in this portfolio are the product of years of development in high-performance sintered magnets, a segment approximately ten times the size of the bonded magnet market,” said Kenji Konishi, Head of Magnet Engineering Production at EM&T. “That development is now in production. We are growing output of grades our customers have already certified, and our SmCo line will be built on the same engineering foundation.”

About Evolution Metals & Technologies Corp.

Evolution Metals & Technologies Corp. (Nasdaq: EMAT) is a U.S.-based critical materials and advanced manufacturing company for rare earth permanent magnets, battery materials, and related critical minerals and technologies. By leveraging proven commercial-scale operations, advanced processing technologies, and strategic partnerships, EM&T operates what it believes is the only vertically integrated critical materials supply chain spanning end-of-life electronics and batteries, high-grade concentrates, and the manufacture of finished rare earth magnets (including high-performance rare earth magnets) and battery materials. For additional information, please visit investors.evolution-metals.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn.

title.rendered: Meet A7 International, an Innovative Global Platform Designed to Reinvent the International Payments Market

content.rendered:
Moscow, Russia, October 13th, 2026, FinanceWire

A7 International enables businesses and individuals to pay invoices with digital assets, while recipients receive a regular bank transfer, reflecting A7’s international positioning and expanding the geography of settlements available to foreign clients.

In two years of operation, A7 has become one of the key players in the international settlements market. Founded in 2024 to serve the foreign economic activity of Russian businesses, it currently serves around 15,000 companies, processing 10+ trillion roubles in 2025 alone. The services A7 offered domestically sparked interest among businesses from other countries, prompting the company to come up with a new product for foreign clients.

The launch of A7 International marks a new stage in A7’s journey. In response to requests from foreign entrepreneurs, the company is expanding its positioning and creating an export offering for businesses in various countries. It is a remote service compliant with local legislation on digital assets and available only in those jurisdictions where cryptocurrency circulation is permitted.

“We are presenting not just a new product in the lineup, but a new image of A7. We have adapted our service so that it can be used remotely from anywhere in the world. This is precisely the key demand of market participants today. They want to be able to transfer money around the world in a few clicks in the shortest possible time – directly from your smartphone, without lengthy paperwork, hidden fees, or unjustified holds on funds. And we are packaging this demand into a convenient and competitive form,” said Chairman of Bank PSB Petr Fradkov.

The mechanics of the service are simple: the client transfers USDT, and A7 arranges a bank transfer via SWIFT using the counterparty details specified in the invoice. The recipient does not need to accept cryptocurrency or open a crypto wallet: the funds arrive in their bank account.

To submit an application, you need to register in your personal account on the website a7.biz. Individuals undergo identity verification (KYC), and companies undergo corporate data verification (KYB). Then the client uploads the invoice and the necessary documents. The built-in algorithm automatically recognizes the invoice data and helps fill out the application.

“The system operates as follows. AI analyzes the sender and beneficiary, jurisdictions, and key risk factors of the transaction. Based on the verification results, a risk profile of the payment is formed and the available options for processing it are determined. The system compares compliance requirements with the capabilities of the existing payment infrastructure. After that, it recommends the optimal payment route taking into account its cost, speed, reliability, and applicable restrictions. Routing dynamically adapts to changes in conditions and the availability of payment channels. Data accumulated over the years makes it possible to continuously improve the quality of decisions made by the system,” noted A7 CEO Ilan Shor.

At launch, A7 International accepts USDT on the TRON network. Bank transfers are available in US dollars, euros, Chinese yuan, and UAE dirhams. Other currencies are available by prior agreement. The commission is 0.3% for both businesses and individuals. After uploading the invoice, the client sees the final cost of the payment, including commission, in advance.
